title: Vitest Reference
description: A quick reminder of the ideas and examples in the Vitest lessons. Open the linked lesson when you need more help.

entries.name: Your first Vitest check
entries.summary: Vitest runs named tests and reports mismatched expectations. It works with JavaScript and TypeScript projects.

example.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("counts apples", () => { expect(3 + 2).toBe(5); });

notes: These imports belong in a Vitest test file, not a plain browser script.

entries.name: Object equality
entries.summary: toEqual compares the values inside an object. It is useful when a function returns a new object.

example.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("returns a point", () => { const point = { x: 2, y: 4 }; expect(point).toEqual({ x: 2, y: 4 }); });

notes: Do not confuse equal fields with the same object identity.

entries.name: Partial object checks
entries.summary: objectContaining checks selected fields when other fields are not part of the current test.

example.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("has a title", () => { expect({ title: "Moon", pages: 24 }).toEqual(expect.objectContaining({ title: "Moon" })); });

notes: A partial match does not prove unmentioned fields are correct.

entries.name: Parameterized tests
entries.summary: test.each repeats one rule for a table of examples. This reduces repeated test code while keeping cases visible.

example.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test.each([[1, 1], [2, 4], [3, 9]])("square %i", (input, expected) => { expect(input * input).toBe(expected); });

notes: A test table should include useful edge cases, not only easy positive inputs.

entries.name: Fresh fixtures
entries.summary: A fixture is prepared data used by a test. beforeEach can give each test a new fixture.
notes: Sharing changed fixture data can make test order matter.

entries.name: Function spies
entries.summary: vi.fn creates a spy that records its calls. You can check the arguments as well as the count.

example.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("notifies with score", () => { const notify = vi.fn(); notify(7); expect(notify).toHaveBeenCalledWith(7); });

notes: A spy should replace a clear boundary, not every line of your own function.

entries.name: Restore a spied method
entries.summary: vi.spyOn watches an existing method. Restore it after the test so later code sees the normal method again.
notes: Clearing recorded calls is not the same as restoring an original method.

entries.name: Async assertions
entries.summary: Use await when checking a promise. The test must stay active until the check is finished.

example.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("reads a label", async () => { const load = async () => "ready"; await expect(load()).resolves.toBe("ready"); });

notes: An unawaited promise can hide a failure after the test finishes.

entries.name: Expected rejected work
entries.summary: A failing promise can be the correct result for invalid input. rejects tests that case explicitly.

example.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("missing book", async () => { await expect(Promise.reject(new Error("No book"))).rejects.toThrow("No book"); });

notes: Do not turn all errors into success just to make a test pass.

entries.name: Fake time
entries.summary: Vitest can replace timers with a controlled clock. This makes a timer test quick and repeatable.

example.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("waits for reminder", () => { vi.useFakeTimers(); try { const remind = vi.fn(); setTimeout(remind, 500); vi.advanceTimersByTime(500); expect(remind).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1); } finally { vi.useRealTimers(); } });

notes: Fake timers should be restored even when an assertion throws.

entries.name: DOM tests need an environment
entries.summary: A Node test has no real browser page. Choose a DOM test environment or browser mode when the behaviour needs page elements.
notes: A DOM simulation does not prove visual layout in a real browser.

entries.name: Use coverage as a clue
entries.summary: Coverage reports which code was reached by tests. Reaching a line does not prove its result was checked well.

example.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("both signs", () => { const positive = n => n > 0; expect(positive(2)).toBe(true); expect(positive(-1)).toBe(false); });

notes: High coverage is not a guarantee of correct behaviour.
